scope: Five canonical entity examples, populated ONLY with values found in committed repository data. No value below was invented. Where a domain has no backing data, its value is null, not a placeholder string — this is itself the point: the canonical model represents absence as null, never as generated filler text, unlike the current live site (see audit/fallback-taxonomy.json).
method: Each example was assembled by directly querying the relevant /data/*.json files and, for the comparison and sibling examples, the actual generated HTML in /compare/ and /names/*/siblings/. Every source is cited per example.

example_1_minimallyPopulated.subject: Abtin (id 32) — chosen because it has zero origin/meaning/popularity/equivalents data of any kind, the modal case for the site's 3,697 names.
_dataGaps: dataCompletenessScore (0.38) = 14 non-null leaf values / 37 total leaf slots in this entity object, counted directly from the JSON below (a non-empty array counts as one populated leaf; a null domain object counts its inner leaves as absent).
metadata.createdAt and metadata.lastUpdated cannot be populated from any current dataset — no repository data tracks per-record timestamps, despite the schema requiring them.

relatedNames.similarNameIds/clusterId are computed at page-render time by generate-programmatic-pages.js and are not persisted anywhere queryable outside of that render — this example reports null rather than re-running that render logic.

example_2_highlyPopulated.subject: Aadi (id 1) — chosen because it has the richest combination of real data found anywhere in the dataset: origin, language, popularity, and a sibling-harmony page.
_dataGaps: dataCompletenessScore (0.51) = 21 non-null leaf values / 41 total leaf slots, same counting method as example_1.
meaning is still null even for this, one of the most-populated names in the dataset — meaning.primary is populated for only 3 of 3,697 names sitewide (audit/knowledge-coverage.json).

relationships.siblingPairs[0].sharedOrigin is null (not false) specifically because scripts/generate-sibling-pages.js computed this from the UNENRICHED data/names.json, which has no origin_cluster for Aadi even though data/names-enriched.json (used for this example's own origin.* fields) does. This null is a direct, faithful illustration of the finding in audit/knowledge-redundancy.json (origin-dual-file-split).

example_3_surname.subject: Campbell — a surname entity. NOTE: this is deliberately NOT expressed using schemas/name-entity.schema.json, because a surname is a different entity type. It is included in the shape a future Surname Entity schema would likely take, built only from real data, to make the Name-vs-Surname boundary concrete (see docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md).

entity.usageNote: Scottish surname; works with first names ending in a vowel or with two syllables.

_dataGaps: No canonical schema exists yet for this entity type — see docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md, 'Domain boundaries', for why Surname was intentionally excluded from Phase 2A's scope.

example_4_comparisonEntity.subject: Aadi: United States vs Canada — a real, live /compare/aadi/us-vs-canada/ page.
sources: compare/aadi/us-vs-canada/index.html (rendered output, since scripts/generate-compare-pages.js computes these values at render time rather than persisting them to any dataset)
_dataGaps: rank2013/movement/delta are null because data/popularity.json contains no year-2013-or-2015 rows for any name — not specific to this comparison.

This single rendered page contains BOTH an honest disclosure ('We do not yet have official rankings for Canada') in its direct-answer lead AND a generic fallback claim ('Rank and movement data are available for our covered countries') later in the same page's trend-delta section — both verified present in compare/aadi/us-vs-canada/index.html in this phase. This example's structured fields reflect the true null data; the page's own text does not consistently do the same, which is exactly the Phase 1C finding this example is drawn from.

example_5_siblingRelationship.subject: Aadi + Aahil — the #1-ranked sibling-harmony recommendation on Aadi's real /names/aadi/siblings/ page.
_dataGaps: scoringFactors.sharedOrigin.value is null despite Aadi having real origin data (India / Sanskrit) in data/names-enriched.json, because the sibling generator never reads that file — the renderedLabel field shows the literal fallback text ('various origins') the live page shows in its place. This is the single clearest concrete instance of the origin-dual-file-split finding (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json) applied to one real, named pair of entities rather than described in the abstract.
